producer: Official Apache OpenCMIS InMemory1.1.0, independent official Java SDK1.1.0
capture: Open the disposable Testcontainers fixture, seed oracle.bin through its SDK with bytes[0,255,17,42,128,9], and independently reread all SDK bytes.

GET repositoryInfo at the explicit repository URL, object and content at the explicit root URL plus the returned opaque objectId; send succinct=false and fixture-only credentials. Require nativeHTTP200 and bound each complete body to1MiB.
Hash original response bytes before fatal UTF8 decoding control bodies; retain their text unchanged. Encode content bytes as base64 and require full equality with the independent SDK original.
Close SDK/server/network through the fixture owner. Regeneration changes random IDs, native timestamps and mapped URLs; retain the new raw-byte hashes rather than normalizing native bodies.
byte_authority: independent.json repository/object.text retain exact native UTF8 bodies. SHA256 applies to UTF8 bytes of those strings, not pretty-printed JSON envelope bytes. content.base64 decodes to exact SDK-verified native content.
benchmark: bench/cmis.bench.ts replays captures with in-memory Fetch. Construction, import, decoding, hashing and complete result preflight are outside sampling. Raw cached-URL Fetch+JSON/arrayBuffer lanes are lower bounds without client request preparation, lossless validation, freezing or extent checks. No live network, deployed provider, SDK speed, throughput or equivalent conformance claim.
response_framing: Only native body/status bytes were captured. The benchmark reconstructs Content-Length from the verified content size; it does not claim original native header or packet timing.
limits: One ordinary6-byte original, one repository-info map, one object envelope; no broad property-size or bulk transfer performance claim.
The archival WAR accepts invalid Basic credentials because no HTTP authentication filter is installed; no native authentication qualification.
Apache Chemistry is retired. Its Apache-2.0 server/SDK and historical dependency graph are isolated test-only artifacts, not production dependencies or an audit.
